claim: Why were sunflowers used after a nuclear disaster?

knots.passage: Helianthus annuus can be used in phytoremediation to extract pollutants from soil such as lead and other heavy metals, such as cadmium, zinc, cesium, strontium, and uranium. The phytoremediation process begins by absorbing the heavy metal(s) through the roots, which gradually accumulate in other areas, such as the shoots and leaves. Helianthus annuus can also be used in rhizofiltration to neutralize radionuclides, such as caesium-137 and strontium-90, from contaminated water, as was done in the case of a pond after the Chernobyl disaster. A similar campaign was mounted in response to the Fukushima Daiichi nuclear disaster.
knots.hatnote: Sunflowers were sent to clean up Chernobyl.

knots.passage: Rhizofiltration is a form of phytoremediation that involves filtering contaminated groundwater, surface water and wastewater through a mass of roots to remove toxic substances or excess nutrients.
knots.hatnote: How do roots remove contaminants from water?

knots.passage: One challenge to phytoremediation is that heavy metals are often insufficiently mobile to be taken up by the plants, hyperaccumulators or otherwise. This challenge prompted the invention of assisted phytoextraction, whereby a chelator is added to soil to increase metal solubility or mobilization so that the plants can absorb them more easily. A typical chelator is edta.
knots.hatnote: What limitation matters when applying plant-based remediation elsewhere?

payoff: Sunflower roots can soak radioactive metals out of water, though plants often need chemical help to reach them.
